Although Jassy did not name Muse during the earnings call, his remarks come amid growing competition between retailers and technology companies over AI-powered shopping.Amazon CEO says AI shopping agents are not a threat yetAcknowledging that Amazon reported weaker-than-expected advertising performance during its third quarter, Andy Jassy told investors that agents were not the cause. He said that consumers still prefer visiting retailers directly rather than relying on external AI assistants to find and purchase products.Other than Amazon, Meta has signed partnerships with Shopify, Walmart, and Best Buy that allows its customers to use Muse. Such tools could potentially change how consumers interact with online retailers and reduce the need to visit individual shopping websites or apps.For Amazon, this could also affect its advertising business. The company's online store relies heavily on product listings and advertisements that customers see while browsing and searching for items. If AI agents begin handling shopping decisions outside its platform, Amazon could lose some of those customer interactions and advertising opportunities.However, Jassy said external shopping agents were no threat.Also, Amazon is developing its own shopping assistant, called Alexa for shopping. During the earnings call, Andy Jassy said more than 400 million customers had used Alexa for shopping over the past year, with customer interactions increasing 570% year over year.
